subject_line: Max the Mastodon and a poet among paleontologists
email_body:
Dear Christina,

I was struck by the origin of The Last Mastodon: a summer as poet-in-residence at a paleontology conference at the Western Science Center in Hemet, with Max the Mastodon and the museum's fossil collection feeding poems about history, assembly and ownership.

I'd love to ask how spending time alongside paleontologists changed the way you think about putting a poem together, bone by bone.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Rattle Chapbook Prize-winning The Last Mastodon (2019) grew from a 2017 poet residency at Western Science Center paleontology conference (Georgia Southern Digital Commons, Rattle); email seen in search result on Georgia Southern creative writing page.
